text: How is ALHQ for EEE211/CSE231 in terms of learning & grading?

comments.label: Comment by Arjun Bordhan 2 weeks ago
Comment by Shaira Tahsin 2 weeks ago
comments.text:
I wouldn't recommend him unless you're able to give 150% of attention in his classes. Sir is very elderly so you might have trouble understanding his classes. That isn't to say he's not a great teacher. In fact he'll teach you theories from scratch and will take time explaining concepts thoroughly. He doesn't use slides tho. Handwritten notes for his class and he'll ask you to read specific topics from the book.
For assessment: 8-10 quizzes. He takes quizzes almost every week but will tell you the questions beforehand. So it's pretty easy to score full marks on them. And they're taken on a single topic. Not full chapters. One of the advantages of this is it helps to stay up to date with classes and it's a lot less pressurizing during mids/finals. He will count best n-2 or even more depending on the class performance. He usually discusses it by the end.
In terms of grading, sir used to curve by 10√x back in our time. I'm not sure if he still does that. But all in all, you'll have to have a lot of mental preparation to keep up with him if you take his course
